question_text: Read the following text and fill in each gap with a
stimulus: suitable word based on the information of the text.15 = 5 Responsibility is the quality or state of being responsible. It is duty or an obligation TO DO something. For example, Board & Test Questions : First Paper you have the responsibility to take care of your parents in their old age, to attend school and pursue your studies properly and so on. You also have responsibility to society and government e.g. to help a neighbour in trouble or to cast your vote if you are 18 or over. A responsibility is also an obligation or a duty NOT TO DO something. For example, you have the responsibility not to steal a book from a public library or not to pile up your building materials on the footpath. These are you responsibilities as citizens. But there are responsibilities of the government as well. Our government has responsibilities to provide for its citizens "the basic necessities of life, including food, clothing, shelter, education and medial care." The government also has the responsibilities to protect the fundamental rights of its citizens to freedom of speech and expression, freedom of the press, freedom or religion, equality of all before law, etc. [Unit-1; Lesson-4] A responsibility (a) ⎯ to an obigation both to do something and not to do something. (b) ⎯ care of our parents in their old age and pursuing our studies properly are two instance of our responsibilities. We also have the duty society and the (c) ⎯ . Helping a neighbour in (d) ⎯ is an example of our duty to society while casting vote if we are 18 or over is an example of our (e) ⎯ to the government. Read the passage and answer the questions 4 and 5. P.B. Shelley (1972-1822) was the most vitally instinct with the pure essence of romantic spirit. He gave himself up most unreservedly to the impulse and inspiration of the romantic spirit. He had imbibed the explosive forces of the French Revolution and championed the causes of revolution and freedom. In every sphere of human life, there is 'however' a melancholic tone in his poetry which springs from his frustation and unfulfilled desires. He pined for an ideal world of beauty, love and freedom but he yearned in vain. His poetry is, however, imbubed with optimism. He sang of millennium when cvils of life would disappear like passage of clouds. Shelley's best qualities are revealed in his prometheus unbound Ode to the West Wind, To a skylark. He is a lyrical genious parexcellence. His poetry is marked by melody and imagery.
